designDirection.title: Kaydence Visual System v1 — the build-agent reference set
designDirection.summary: Five logo directions plus ten screen-family boards, each rendered for macOS, Windows, and Linux (30 OS-specific views) sharing one interface system. Generated with Codex from Plan of Attack v3, the Whisper-Ahead v2 interaction, and the monorepo PRD/ARCHITECTURE/ROADMAP, then adopted as the canonical UI/UX/visual source of truth for every screen built from P1 onward. Screen layout is fixed by the boards; the only free-tier per-OS variation is the selection accent (macOS aqua / Windows cobalt / Linux emerald).

designDirection.openDecision: RESOLVED 2026-07-08 (ADR-0012 Accepted): dual-asset identity — Option 1 K Waveform is the sole product mark (app icon, favicon, tray monochrome variant, installers, all isolated use); Option 4 Wordmark Forward is the Kaydence wordmark/site header with its serif as brand display type only. Binding rules: strict role separation (never substitute or compose the two as twin logos); Option 4's icon variant retired; serif never inside the app UI. Options 2/5 remain secondary art (privacy seal; Relay fleet illustration); Option 3 rejected (embeds third-party OS marks). The Option 1 mark fills the reserved slot on every screen.

invariants: One consistent left navigation across every screen: Dictate, Whisper-Ahead, Cleanup, Relay, Voiceprint, Conductor, Privacy, Dictionary, Analytics, Setup.
Card radius stays 8px; components are compact cards, tables, segmented controls, toggles, icon buttons, status badges, small charts, and native OS permission panels.
Prediction suggestions render blue in every theme; an accepted prediction pulses amber-gold for roughly 0.5s then settles to normal text.
Destructive Conductor actions always require an explicit confirm gate.
Never imply cloud sync for core features; Harbor is an optional hosted service only, and every Harbor service has a self-hostable path.
All controls keyboard-reachable, readable at high OS scaling, with no text overlap at narrow desktop widths.
Default, light, and dark modes exist for every OS; only the single free-tier accent differs by OS lane; premium theme expansion may add colors later without changing layout.

Identity (ADR-0012): Option 1 K Waveform is the only mark; Option 4 is the only wordmark (site/marketing serif only). Never substitute or pair them as twin logos; no serif inside the app UI; no second icon. Violations fail the phase fidelity gates.

mission.name: Kaydence — Plan of Attack v3
mission.tagline: Speak anywhere. Ship clean text. Never leak, never lose, never lag.
mission.northStar: Own the machine, the voice, and the fleet: a local-first dictation platform whose flagship trio (Voiceprint, Relay, Conductor) no cloud incumbent can copy without abandoning its business model. Privacy line = transmission + persistence, not awareness (ADR-0006). Pay-once, three desktops, one behavior.

tasks.title: PRD P0-2 Local ASR dual path (Parakeet V3 CPU + Whisper large-v3-turbo GPU; model picker; hw auto-recommend)
tasks.notes: MODEL READINESS + PICKER + SELECTION PERSISTENCE + DOWNLOAD PLANNING/METADATA UI + MISMATCH QUARANTINE + MANUAL RECHECK + PENDING RUNTIME ADAPTER WIRED 2026-07-08: app startup loads the source-tree model registry and verifies required first-run ASR/VAD artifacts in the app-data models directory. AppSnapshot exposes model_ready, model_readiness_error, required_models, ASR candidates, recommended_asr_model_id, selected_asr_model_id, and download_available/download_size_mb/download_source_count for model rows. The first-run UI renders the backend-owned local ASR picker and required-model list with validated download size/source metadata, invokes select_asr_model, and exposes Recheck Models; Rust validates the selected candidate, persists selected_asr_model_id to app-data/settings.json, reapplies it on startup, and returns the updated AppSnapshot. The refresh_model_readiness Tauri command rescans app-data models without restart and reapplies persisted ASR selection. Placeholder hashes fail closed, missing valid artifacts render as download-required only when ModelDownloadPlan can prove a safe destination, expected sha256, and normalized HTTPS source list; TODO/invalid sources block readiness as Download unavailable. Checksum mismatches move the suspect artifact into models/quarantine/ before blocking readiness, and the recommendation rule prefers OS-specific registry defaults then CPU-safe Parakeet-style fallback. The default hotkey runtime now uses a PendingLocalAsrEngine, so captures persist audio and record a selected-model-specific Recognize failure instead of a generic empty-stack error until real Parakeet/Whisper adapters load. REMAINING: replace TODO registry hashes/sources with real published artifacts, implement the network fetch/progress UI, Parakeet/Whisper engine adapters, hot-swap adapter lifecycle, and WER/latency evidence.

tasks.title: PRD P0-3 Universal injection Mac+Win+Linux (AX / UIA+SendInput / X11+Wayland; clipboard fallback snapshot-restore <=200ms; secure-field refusal)
tasks.notes: LINUX uinput KEYSTROKE BACKEND BUILT + VALIDATED (2026-07-08): inject/uinput.rs — pure US-QWERTY keymap (5 tests, CI) + UinputKeyboard (evdev 0.13) creating a /dev/uinput virtual keyboard. Live PASS on the VM: device at /dev/input/event5, emitted 19+26-char strings. atspi-selftest focus-track = the REAL integrated path (AT-SPI secure-field GATE + uinput TYPING). Operator demo: scripts/linux-inject-demo.sh. REMAINING for the Linux leg: the human-focus end-to-end check (focus a field -> types; focus a password -> refuses) is operator-in-the-loop (Wayland won't let a script move keyboard focus). THEN: unicode-beyond-ASCII typing (compose/keymap-swap, follow-up), the portal+libei alternative to uinput (no device perm), macOS AX, Windows UIA, hotkey OS registration. Earlier context below. LINUX INJECTION — LIVE FINDINGS ON THE GNOME VM (2026-07-08) reshaped the strategy: (1) AT-SPI connect/traverse/READ + role/state detection WORK on GNOME (validated: found gnome-text-editor role=Text editable field). (2) AT-SPI EditableText.InsertText is UNRELIABLE on modern GNOME — returns true but no-ops on gnome-text-editor (GTK4) AND gedit 44. So AT-SPI = the DETECTION / secure-field signal (non-negotiable #8, the part that works), NOT the primary insertion path. (3) uinput keystroke synth (ydotool, daemonless on /dev/uinput) is the working inject path. REVISED LADDER (docs/spikes §7b + ADR-0013 amendment): detect via AT-SPI, INSERT via keystroke (uinput or portal+libei). NEXT: implement the uinput/portal keystroke backend behind KeystrokeChannel::LinuxUinput/WaylandPortalRemoteDesktop, wire AT-SPI secure-field detection as the gate; the end-to-end 'types into focused app' check is operator-in-the-loop (Wayland won't let a script move keyboard focus). Then macOS AX + Windows UIA. Evidence: P1-P0-3-atspi-live-findings-2026-07-08.txt. Earlier context below. LINUX AT-SPI FOUNDATION VALIDATED ON THE VM (2026-07-08): ADR-0013 Accepted; atspi 0.30 + zbus 5 added (cfg linux, pure D-Bus, audit-network PASS); inject/linux.rs role->FieldKind mapping (PasswordText=>Secure, tested); bin/atspi-selftest connects to real GNOME and round-trips a call (desktop root role=DesktopFrame, PASS — evidence P1-P0-3-atspi-validated-2026-07-08.txt). NEXT ITERATION: focus tracking (object:state-changed:focused) -> read focused role/state for secure detection -> EditableText.insert_text native insert, then operator-observed live validation (type into GNOME Text Editor; refuse a password entry). Then macOS AX + Windows UIA backends. Earlier context below. SPIKE DONE (Wayland-first, 2026-07-08): docs/spikes/P1-P0-3-wayland-injection.md maps the compositor matrix + strategy (capability ladder: AT-SPI native -> portal/libei on GNOME/KDE, virtual-keyboard on wlroots, uinput opt-in, clipboard-restore). Platform-agnostic CORE implemented + unit-tested on host (inject/mod.rs: decide_secure, select_plan, clipboard_paste, outcome_event, TextInjector trait — 13 tests, all 3 CI legs green). Honest finding: Wayland has no global secure-field signal for opaque (non-AT-SPI) clients — policy makes it explicit (Lenient flags unverified / Strict refuses). ADR-0013 PROPOSED — HALTS for operator go on the dependency set (atspi/ashpd+libei/wayland-client/x11rb) before platform syscalls are written + validated on the Debian-12 GNOME VM. Non-negotiable #8 secure-field refusal is the load-bearing tested gate.

Exit: all three daily-usable across the fleet; ladder targets hit; Harbor optional and unbuilt without blocking anything.

risks.title: Wayland secure-field detection gap on opaque clients
risks.note: Non-AT-SPI Wayland apps expose no password-field signal — Kaydence cannot always confirm a field is non-secure (ADR-0013 §secure-field). Mitigated: default Lenient flags the result unverified (UI warns per app, board 07); opt-in Strict refuses opaque focus. A real platform limitation, surfaced to the user rather than papered over.

Remaining is live OS permission/conflict/rebind proof, toggle/rebind UI, and full P1-G2/P1-G3 gates.

P1-P0-2 model readiness/picker: STARTED — AppSnapshot now loads the registry, exposes required ASR/VAD model states, ASR candidates, selected/recommended model ids, and validated download metadata (available/size/source count), and the first-run UI renders the local ASR picker + required-model list from that backend truth. select_asr_model validates candidates, persists selected_asr_model_id in app-data/settings.json, and reapplies it on startup. refresh_model_readiness rescans app-data models and reapplies persisted ASR selection so first-run can recheck newly installed artifacts without restart. Current registry TODO checksums correctly block readiness; missing models only show Download required when ModelDownloadPlan has a safe destination, expected sha256, and HTTPS sources; checksum mismatches quarantine the suspect artifact before blocking load. The default hotkey runtime now carries a PendingLocalAsrEngine keyed to the selected ASR model/lane, so it records an honest selected-model-specific Recognize failure instead of a generic empty-stack failure until real adapters land. Next real work is replacing TODO hashes/sources with reviewed artifacts, implementing the network fetch/progress UI, building Parakeet/Whisper engine adapters, and adding the adapter hot-swap lifecycle.

conventions: One work unit = one branch (mission/<phaseId>-<slug>) = one merge; <=400 changed lines.
Run the internal loop per prompts/BUILD-LOOP.md (ORIENT->PLAN->BUILD->JUDGE->AUDIT->GATE) inside each task; mission-control governs phases/state/reporting above it.
No authority without evidence: every 'done' has an artifact saved under ops/mission/evidence/.
A green Judge with a red Audit does not merge.
Critical decision paths (JUDGE-AUDITOR.md) HALT for operator go + ADR — never merge one silently.
Heartbeat after every merge: update state.json, run node ops/mission/render-sotu.mjs, append journal.md, commit state+journal+HTML.

Never weaken a non-negotiable to pass a gate — that is itself a blocking defect.
